summary: RePORTER's default search surface includes a machine-generated concept tag list, and its results mix procurement contracts and NIH intramural projects with grants, so an amount-sorted keyword search answers neither 'what work is funded here' nor 'how much does this topic get': the CLI must restrict search_field to title and abstract, whitelist applicable activity codes, send the amount floor as a request criterion, and report a median alongside the size-sorted listing.
reason: The 'terms' field is attached to every project independently of its subject, so a building management award matches a disease keyword and outranks real research on amount. Activity codes must be filtered server-side because the API accepts the criterion and a client-side pass would discard most of each page. The amount floor cannot be applied after the fact: the API returns the largest awards first, so a post-filter only removes rows and never pulls smaller matching awards into view. The median must be located by counting awards above a series of thresholds rather than by sampling a page, because the distribution is heavily right-skewed and any single page is a biased slice. A regen that restores search_field=all, drops the activity code whitelist, or estimates the median from returned rows reintroduces results that look like an NIH data problem rather than a client one. max_amount must also stay below 2,147,483,647: above it RePORTER returns an empty-body HTTP 500 that is indistinguishable from an outage.
validated_outcome: FY2024 'cancer' sorted by award: largest result fell from $366,260,951 (a library services project) to $2,833,086, and grants an external applicant can compete for rose from 1 of the top 25 to 25 of 25. Reported typical award $450,000 in the $400,000-$500,000 bracket, matching an independent threshold probe of the API; sampling the 300 smallest matching rows instead gave $34,465.
